root_cause.text: In move_pages_huge_pmd(), the code sets src_folio to NULL for the huge zero page path and then calls folio_mk_pmd(NULL, ...), which dereferences NULL via folio_pfn() and page_to_pfn(), leading to a bogus PFN (on SPARSEMEM_VMEMMAP) or NULL dereference (on other memory models); additionally, reconstructing the PMD from the folio instead of preserving the original PMD state drops the pmd_special flag, causing vm_normal_page_pmd() to treat the moved huge zero PMD as a normal page and corrupt its refcount.
root_cause.evidence: From the CVE description: "src_folio is NULL, so folio_mk_pmd(NULL, pgprot) passes NULL through folio_pfn() and page_to_pfn(). With SPARSEMEM_VMEMMAP this silently produces a bogus PFN, installing a PMD pointing to non-existent physical memory. On other memory models it is a NULL dereference." Also: "move_pages_huge_pmd() currently reconstructs the destination PMD in the huge zero page branch, which drops PMD state such as pmd_special() ... As a result, vm_normal_page_pmd() can treat the moved huge zero PMD as a normal page and corrupt its refcount." The patch replaces the folio_mk_pmd() call with deriving the destination PMD from the original PMD value after clearing, preserving special flags.

Clears the original PMD and stores its value, but the stored value is not used to preserve flags like pmd_special when reconstructing the PMD, contributing to the loss of special flags.

Directly vulnerable: when src_folio is NULL for huge zero page, this call dereferences NULL via folio_pfn()/page_to_pfn() and also drops pmd_special by creating a new PMD from the folio instead of preserving the original PMD state.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly dereferences NULL via src_folio when handling huge zero page, causing folio_pfn() and page_to_pfn() to produce bogus PFN or NULL pointer dereference. It also reconstructs the PMD from the folio instead of preserving the original PMD state, losing the pmd_special flag.

Commits the defective _dst_pmd into the page table, making the vulnerability effective: either installing a PMD with bogus PFN (leading to NULL dereference on access) or a PMD missing the pmd_special flag (causing refcount corruption when vm_normal_page_pmd() treats it as a normal page).

Clears the original PMD and stores its value, but the stored src_pmdval is not used to preserve important flags like pmd_special when reconstructing the destination PMD. This contributes to the loss of special page characteristics.
This else branch is the execution path taken for the huge zero page case. Its presence leads to the subsequent vulnerable code that sets src_folio to NULL and calls folio_mk_pmd(NULL, ...).

While part of the non-zero page path, this line is part of the same PMD manipulation logic within the function. If the conditional logic were flawed, this line could also be involved in improper PMD handling, though the main vulnerability lies in the else branch.

Current implementation of UFFDIO_MOVE fails to move zeropages and ret
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit eb1521dad8f391d3f3b88f589db27a288b55b8ed
Author: Suren Baghdasaryan <surenb@google.com>
Date:   Wed Jan 31 09:56:18 2024 -0800

    userfaultfd: handle zeropage moves by UFFDIO_MOVE
    
    Current implementation of UFFDIO_MOVE fails to move zeropages and returns
    EBUSY when it encounters one.  We can handle them by mapping a zeropage at
    the destination and clearing the mapping at the source.  This is done both
    for ordinary and for huge zeropages.
    
    Link: https://lkml.k
bic_trace_step.reason: In the huge zero page path (else branch after the is_huge_zero_pmd check), the code reconstructs the destination PMD using mk_huge_pmd(src_page, dst_vma->vm_page_prot) instead of preserving the original PMD value from src_pmdval. This drops the pmd_special flag from the PMD entry, so subsequent calls to vm_normal_page_pmd() will treat the moved huge zero PMD as a normal page and corrupt its refcount. The NULL dereference via folio_mk_pmd(NULL,...) is not present because mk_huge_pmd is used with the zero page pointer; however, the missing preservation of the special flag is the core vulnerability described. No fix is applied in this commit.
